title: Deconvolution: capacity drift analysis and protective fleet policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a mid-week traffic surge on 2026-02-24 we observed a progressive capacity shortfall in multiple Dedicated pools serving enterprise customers. The incident manifested as rising queue latencies, increased request timeouts against P95/P99 SLAs, and eventual request rejects when headroom hit circuit thresholds. This ticket captures the forensics, immediate mitigations, and a set of durable fleet policies and automation to prevent recurrence.

Scope: Affected 3 dedicated regions (us-west-2-dedicated, eu-central-1-dedicated, ap-southeast-1-dedicated) and ~12 customer accounts with reserved capacity. Root of the regression was tied to a recent autoscaler change and an interaction with the headroom accounting logic introduced in runtime-1.20. Impact window: ~2026-02-24 09:05 UTC -> 2026-02-24 13:40 UTC.

Why this matters: Dedicated customers expect throughput guarantees and predictable tail latency; the event resulted in degraded user experience for customers on committed capacity and generated elevated support noise and remediation costs.
timeline:
2026-02-24 08:58 UTC: Canary alerts (headroom < 15%) triggered for us-west-2-dedicated.
2026-02-24 09:05 UTC: Autoscaler chains started to back off; scale-up acknowledgements delayed by 45-90s due to a new debounce path.
2026-02-24 09:27 UTC: Queue depths increase; Redis circuit engaged for KV-prefetch; fallback to cold path increases p99.
2026-02-24 10:02 UTC: First customer reports to SRE and CSMs.
2026-02-24 10:15 UTC: Incident declared. Emergency throttle and temporary overprovision requested.
2026-02-24 10:34 UTC: Manual override: forced allocation of 8x warm units to top 3 affected pools; immediate latency improvement observed.
2026-02-24 11:20 UTC: Rollback of autoscaler debounce change (reverting commit) completed.
2026-02-24 12:50 UTC: Headroom metrics normalized; queues drained.
2026-02-24 13:40 UTC: Incident transitioned to post-incident analysis phase.
root_cause: Primary cause: a change in the autoscaler (commit ab12f7) introduced a debounce window that suppressed scale-up signals when transient token-generation latency spikes occurred; this was combined with a subtle change in headroom accounting (runtime-1.20) where KV-cache warmup contributions were no longer counted towards available headroom for dedicated pools. In practice the autoscaler underestimated required replicas during sustained high-concurrency tail workloads, causing slower reaction and headroom depletion. Secondary cause: alert thresholds were tuned for steady-state CPU signals and did not capture rapid queueing at the request router layer.
mitigations:
Immediate: 1) Reverted the debounce change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1839). 2) Forced allocation of additional warm units to affected dedicated pools and temporarily increased soft headroom reserve from 10% to 25%. 3) Applied emergency throttles for low-priority background workloads.
Near-term (2 weeks): 1) Adjust rate of autoscaler decision loop and add a short-circuit for sustained queue growth. 2) Reintroduce KV-cache contribution to headroom accounting for dedicated pools. 3) Add a dedicated highly-visible dashboard for 'queue depth by pool' with alert runbooks.
Long-term (quarter): 1) Implement predictive-autoscaling prototype (based on short-window trend detection) as a canary feature behind a flag. 2) Formalize dedicated-pool SLA-preservation policies: automated temporary overprovision, per-customer graceful degradation, and cross-region spillover policy. 3) End-to-end load tests for headroom/outage scenarios integrated into CI.

ENG-A2: Rework headroom accounting to include KV-cache warmup for Dedicated pools - owner: Sofia Ramirez - estimate: 5
ENG-A3: Add emergency overprovision automation (policy: allocate extra warm units when headroom < 20%) - owner: Daniel Okafor - estimate: 5
ENG-A4: Create a runbook and SLO-linked alert for rapid queue growth (include customer escalation path) - owner: Priya Singh - estimate: 2
ENG-A5: Schedule chaos tests that spike token-generation latency to validate scale-up paths - owner: SRE Team - estimate: 3
ENG-A6: Postmortem write-up and customer communication draft - owner: Aisha Patel - estimate: 1
